question: Why can the largest patterns on the cosmic background never be measured much more precisely than they are now?
options: Only one sky exists to sample
Galactic dust hides them for good
answer: Only one sky exists to sample. The largest patterns span a quarter of the sky or more, so there are only a handful: five at the very largest scale. Measured perfectly, they are still five draws from chance. Planck has reached that limit; an odd pattern there can never be retested on a fresh sky.
move: When the sample is everything there is, no instrument adds certainty.
ask: Where am I asking for more certainty than this question can give?
trap: Blaming foreground dust, which better maps could in principle remove.
reference: Dodelson & Schmidt, Modern Cosmology, 2nd ed., Academic Press, 2020
